articles.title: Maharashtra Govt plans 'Jalyukt Shivar' in 18,000 villages amid severe drought - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Maharashtra Govt plans 'Jalyukt Shivar' in 18,000 villages amid severe drought The New Indian Express
articles.content: With nearly 90 per cent of Maharashtra facing drought conditions amid the impact of El Niño, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has directed all government departments to intensify water conservation efforts and ensure maximum harvesting of rainwater to strengthen groundwater reserves. The CM also directed officials to implement the third phase of the Jalyukt Shivar scheme, Jalyukt Shivar 3.0, across 18,000 villages.At a review meeting on the progress of the ‘Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain 2026’ campaign, Fadnavis announced an ambitious target of creating 34,83,940 groundwater recharge structures across the state by May 2027. The meeting was chaired by Union Jal Shakti Minister CR Patil, who joined online.He called for the convergence of funds and ongoing work under various central and state government schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and VB-G RAM G, to ensure effective implementation of water conservation projects.Emphasising the need for a coordinated approach, Fadnavis instructed all departments to work under the supervision of district collectors and prepare time-bound action plans for water conservation in their respective districts..Maharashtra adds six talukas to drought-hit list, total rises to 310.The proposed measures include the construction of check dams and ponds, large-scale rooftop rainwater harvesting in private and government buildings, and the rejuvenation of rivers extending over 50 kilometres that remain seasonal and carry water primarily during the monsoon.The CM stressed that rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge should become priorities at every level of administration, particularly in drought-affected regions. He called for the effective utilisation of available funds and closer coordination between departments to ensure that water conservation works are completed within stipulated deadlines.Fadnavis directed officials to accelerate the utilisation of funds under the scheme and ensure that the targeted 50 per cent milestone is achieved by December.The success of the programme, however, will depend on timely execution, effective coordination between departments, availability of funds and monitoring of the completed structures..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: Indian sports wrap, November 19: Tvesa wins final leg of WPGT after dramatic play-off with Ridhima - Sportstar
articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 19: Tvesa wins final leg of WPGT after dramatic play-off with Ridhima Sportstar
articles.content: CHENNAI GOLF Tvesa Malik wins final leg of WPGT after dramatic play-off with Ridhima Dilawari Tvesa Malik held her nerve in a tense finish to close the 2026 Women’s Pro Golf Tour season with a win in the 15th and final leg in Noida on Thursday. This was Tvesa’s second win of the season as she joined Ridhima Dilawari (four wins), Vani Kapoor (two) and Jasmine Shekar (two) as multiple winners in the 2026 season. Tvesa, who began the final round two shots behind Ridhima, carded a 1-under 70 to finish at four-under 209, matching Ridhima, who returned a 72. The title was decided on the second play-off hole, where Tvesa produced a birdie on the par-5 to clinch the win. Amateur Aida Thimmaiah finished tied third alongside Riya Jadon at one-under 212. Aida carded a 71 in the final round, while Riya also closed with a 72, leaving both three shots behind the leading pair. Aida’s steady performance over three rounds also saw her finish among the leading contenders in a field that featured several experienced professionals. Sneha Singh finished fifth at two-over 215 after a 72. - PTI PGA of America develop a PGA-branded golf facility in India The PGA of America announced a partnership with Vimtra Ventures to develop a PGA-branded golf community in India on Thursday. The planned development will combine a designed golf facility and residential community, creating an access to PGA-inspired golf programming, coaching, player development initiatives and premium golf amenities. The initial facility is scheduled to open in 2029 in Chennai along the southeastern coast of India. Beyond the golf course and residential development, it will incorporate PGA coaching programs, player engagement initiatives, junior golf experiences, educational resources, and PGA Professional career opportunities to support the long-term growth of the game throughout India. -Team Sportstar Habitat Charity Golf concludes seventh edition in Mumbai, aims to build homes for 43 tribal families in Palghar The seventh edition saw 88 golfers drawn from the world of business, entrepreneurship, sports and philanthropy take to the course to raise awareness and support for the construction of new homes for 43 tribal families in Modgaon village in Palghar district, Maharashtra. Corporate leaders taking part in the tournament included Mr. Harsh Mariwala, Chairman, Marico Ltd; Mr. Arjun Nohwar, Managing Director, South Asia, Skydance and Mr. John Wilcox, CEO, Navnit Group, Mr. Ajit Agarkar, former Chair, Selection Committee, BCCI and former Indian Cricketer, Mr. S. Badrinath, former Indian Cricketer, Commentator and Coach among others. - Team Sportstar Yuvraj joins Om Prakash and Raunil in three-way lead in Digboi Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh, Mhow’s Om Prakash Chouhan and Bengaluru’s Raunil Kukar shared the 54-hole lead at 11-under 205 after the third round of the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf, a Rs 1 crore event being played in Digboi, Assam. Overnight joint leader Chouhan (67-68-70), 40, carded a two-under 70 featuring six birdies, a double-bogey on the par-3 10th and two bogeys to retain his share of the lead. Kukar (70-65-70), the other overnight joint leader, also returned a two-under 70 comprising five birdies and three bogeys to remain at the top. Yuvraj (68-70-67), who began the day tied fourth and three shots off the lead, fired a five-under 67 featuring seven birdies and two bogeys to join the overnight leaders. He made six of his birdies in two sets of three consecutive holes, first from the fifth to seventh and then from the 14th to 16th. Bangladesh’s Md Razu (69-70-68) climbed from tied eighth to fourth at nine-under 207 following a four-under 68 featuring five birdies and a lone bogey on the par-4 eighth. Mumbai’s Aryaman Aditya Mohan (73-70-65) made the biggest move of the day, climbing from tied 25th to tied fifth at eight-under 208 with a seven-under 65 featuring an eagle on the par-5 seventh, eight birdies and three bogeys. - PTI BADMINTON Junior Nationals: Favourites Shaina Manimuthu, Parul Choudhary book semifinal berth; Bornil beats world bronze medallist Jagsher Top seed Shaina Manimuthu and second seed Parul Choudhary registered contrasting victories to reach the girls’ singles semifinals while Bornil Changmai defeated world junior championships bronze medallist Jagsher Singh Khangurra in boys’ singles quarterfinals of the 49th National Junior (U-19) Badminton Championships in Gangtok on Thursday. Shaina, the defending champion, had to work hard in the opening game before beating Rishika Nandi 16-14, 15-11 while Parul packed off fifth seed Dianka Waldia 15-9, 15-7 in the quarterfinals. Shaina will now take on sixth seed Diksha SR, who defeated Sneha Lamba 15-8, 15-7 in the other quarterfinals. The other semifinal will pit eighth seed Lakshya Rajesh against Parul after the former came from a game down to beat Anvi Rathore 13-15, 15-9, 16-14. In the boys’ singles category, second seed Bornil held his nerves to beat Jagsher 15-10, 13-15, 15-13 to reach the semifinals. Meanwhile, Sparsh Sood’s giant-killing run came to an end at the quarterfinals stage. The unseeded shuttler, who had upset top seed Nishchal Anand in the previous round, went down 15-13, 11-15, 15-10 against Rudra Pratap Singh Rana. Seventh seed Gnana Dattu TT also booked his semifinal berth with a 15-12, 12-15, 15-8 win over third seed Abhinav Garg. Important results Boys’ singles: 7-Gnana Dattu TT bt 3-Abhinav Garg 15-12, 12-15, 15-8; Rudra Pratap Singh Rana bt Sparsh Sood 15-13, 11-15, 15-10 Girls’ singles: 6-Diksha SR bt Sneha Lamba 15-8, 15-7; 1-Shaina Manimuthu bt 13-Rishika Nandi 16-14, 15-11; 8-Lakshya Rajesh bt Anvi Rathore 13-15, 15-9, 16-14; 2-Parul Choudhary bt 5-Dianka Waldia 15-9, 15-7 Mixed Doubles: 3-Punith S/Deepak Taj Aditi bt Malsawmhlua/Zoramthari Renthlei 15-11, 15-10; Amith Raj Natraj/Suhina Roy bt Vedansh Negi/Alisha Bhandari 15-7, 15-11 - Team Sportstar HOCKEY Punjab Hockey League 2026 gets underway in Mohali The third edition of the Punjab Hockey League (PHL) got underway at the Olympian Balbir Singh Sr. International Hockey Stadium in Mohali on Thursday. Indian Men’s Hockey Team vice-captain and PHL 2026 ambassador Hardik Singh graced the occasion, setting the tone for the season as host Roundglass Hockey Academy took to the turf and secured a commanding 3-0 victory over Republican Sports Club, Mumbai. Alongside Hardik, the dignitaries in attendance included Sarpal Singh (Dronacharya Awardee and Founding Director, Roundglass), Dilpreet Singh (Tokyo 2020 Olympic Bronze Medallist and India International), Rajpal Singh (former India hockey captain) and Rajinder Singh Sr. (Moscow 1980 Olympic Gold Medallist, Dronacharya Awardee, and Technical Lead, Roundglass Hockey Academy). In the first match of the day, Ghumanhera Risers Academy, New Delhi, made an emphatic start to its campaign with a dominant 7-2 victory over Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT). In the second match, Naval Tata Hockey Academy, Jamshedpur, edged past Surjit Hockey Academy, Jalandhar, 1-0 in a tightly contested battle. Featuring ten top academy teams from across India competing in a league-cum-knockout format, the league phase runs until December 3 before the knockouts move to the Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar, with the semifinals on December 5 and the grand finale slated for December 6. - Team Sportstar TABLE TENNIS Third National Ranking Table Tennis Championships: Rishaan, Tanishka claim U-15 titles Rishaan Chattopadhyay of West Bengal and Tanishka Kalbhairav of Karnataka justified their top-seeded status to claim the Under-15 Boys’ and Girls’ singles titles respectively at the third National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Phagwara on Thursday. While Rishaan battled back from two games down to edge second seed and fellow Bengal player Himon Mondal 3-2 in a thrilling final, Tanishka dominated her title clash against third seed Myraa Sangelkar of Maharashtra, winning in straight games. Rishaan, who appeared to be on the verge of defeat after dropping the first two games 6-11 and 9-11, mounted a spirited comeback, taking the next two 11-6 and 11-4 to force a decider. The fifth game went down to the wire, with Rishaan holding his nerve to prevail 12-10 after Himon conceded two crucial points on consecutive shots that went out. Tanishka, meanwhile, kept Myraa under pressure from the outset, taking the opening game 11-5 before maintaining her control to win the next two 11-7, 11-8 and seal the title 3-0. Earlier, the U-15 boys’ and girls’ singles events featured several absorbing contests, offering comeback victories and closely fought quarterfinals and semifinals. In the boys’ section, Himon delivered one of the day’s best performances, recovering from two games down to defeat Lakshya Kiumar of UP 3-2 in the quarterfinals. He then overcame Ahan Gosar of Maharashtra 3-1 in the semifinals, with the opening and third games going to 12-10 and 14-12, respectively. RESULTS Boys U-15 Singles: Final: Rishaan Chattopadhyay (WB) beat Himon Mondal (WB) 6-11, 9-11, 11-6, 11-4, 12-10.
